typical_topologies: Point-to-point (Figure 1-7 / Section 8.9) — one MASTER + one SLAVE; signals routed directly; simplest interconnect.

Shared bus (Figure 1-8/1-9 / Section 8.10) — single bus shared between multiple MASTERs and SLAVEs; supports both Multiplexor and Three-State variants (Section 8.10.2). Full or Partial address decoding (Section 8.10.4). System Arbiter chosen by integrator (Section 8.10.5).
Crossbar switch (Figure 1-4 / Section 1.7) — parallel channels between multiple MASTERs and SLAVEs; aggregate throughput by parallel operation; supports both static and dynamic configuration.
Data flow interconnection (Figure 1-5 / Section 1.7) — IP cores arranged in a sequential pipeline; each core has both SLAVE input and MASTER output; concurrency via pipeline parallelism.
Off-chip interconnection (Figure 1-6) — Wishbone interface extends off-chip; same protocol but typically lower clock frequency.

interconnect_role.INTERCON: WISHBONE module that physically interconnects MASTER and SLAVE interfaces (combinational + sequential glue logic). Routes CLK_O -> all CLK_I, RST_O -> all RST_I; routes per-cycle ADR_O/DAT_O/WE_O/SEL_O/STB_O/CYC_O/TAGN_O from MASTER -> SLAVE, and ACK_O/ERR_O/RTY_O/DAT_O/TAGN_O from SLAVE -> MASTER. INTERCON also implements address decoding (full or partial), arbitration (in multi-MASTER topologies), bus combination (multiplexor or three-state per integrator choice), and OPTIONAL watchdog timers (RECOMMENDATION 3.10).
interconnect_role.SYSCON: Drives the bus clock [CLK_O] and reset [RST_O]; one SYSCON per WISHBONE system. SUGGESTION 3.00 — SYSCON should assert [RST_O] during power-up.
interconnect_role.arbiter: End-user-defined arbitration logic (priority arbiter, round-robin arbiter, etc.). Often uses [CYC_I] to select between MASTER interfaces (OBSERVATION on page 28). [LOCK_O] used by MASTER to hold ownership.
interconnect_role.default_slave: Not explicitly mandated by the spec, but recommended for completeness — INTERCON SHOULD return [ERR_I] or [RTY_I] for accesses to unmapped addresses (RECOMMENDATION 3.10 watchdog also helps).

interconnect_rules: All MASTER and SLAVE [CLK_I]/[RST_I] connect to SYSCON via INTERCON.
MASTER [CYC_O] asserted before / with [STB_O], negated after / with [STB_O] (RULE 3.25).
Standard mode: SLAVE [ACK_O]/[ERR_O]/[RTY_O] driven from AND of [CYC_I] AND [STB_I] (RULE 3.35).
Pipelined mode: SLAVE [STALL_O] used by SLAVE to throttle MASTER (Section 3.1.3.2).
INTERCON SHOULD watchdog [STB_O] (RECOMMENDATION 3.10) and disconnect persistently misbehaving interfaces.
All WISHBONE interface signals MUST use active HIGH logic (RULE 2.30).
Address decoding may be Full or Partial (Section 8.10.4); Partial is preferred for SoC (less redundant logic).
Tags ([TGA_O], [TGD_O], [TGD_I], [TGC_O], [TGC_I]) are propagated end-to-end by INTERCON when implemented; integrator wires them per the IP's DATASHEET.

Three-state bus combination (8.10.2) requires technology that supports three-state I/O (typically ASIC top-level pads or FPGA-internal three-state); modern FPGA internal logic typically uses multiplexors instead.

default_signal_values.ERR_O_when_absent: 0 (LOW) — SLAVE does not implement error termination
default_signal_values.STALL_O_when_absent: 0 (LOW) — slave is not stalled (standard mode SLAVE)
default_signal_values.CTI_O_when_absent: 3'b000 (Classic cycle) — backwards compatibility with non-Registered-Feedback cores (RULE 4.10; PERMISSION 4.10 — VHDL CTI_I default '000')
default_signal_values.BTE_O_when_absent: 2'b00 (Linear burst) — when CTI does not indicate incrementing burst
default_signal_values.SEL_O_when_granularity_eq_portsize: All bits HIGH — the entire bus is selected

id_routing.description: Wishbone B4 does NOT define a Manager-ID concept like AHB5 HMASTER or AXI AxID. In multi-MASTER systems, the INTERCON's arbiter tracks which MASTER won the bus and routes the response back accordingly.
id_routing.implication: Wishbone is inherently single-outstanding per MASTER (Classic) or in-order per MASTER (pipelined). Out-of-order routing requires user-defined extensions outside the spec.

guaranteed: All beats of a BLOCK / RMW / Registered-Feedback burst are presented to the same SLAVE in order; CYC_O held throughout.
Pipelined-mode: requests in order, ACKs in order — FIFO behavior.
Locked sequences ([LOCK_O]=1) are not interrupted by other MASTERs in multi-MASTER configurations.
not_guaranteed: Multi-MASTER arbitration order across different cycles is user-defined (arbiter-specific).
AXI-style out-of-order completion (Wishbone has none in B4).

memory_vs_peripheral_regions.wishbone_memory_slave: Synchronous RAM/ROM model (Section 8.7 / FASM); supports SINGLE / BLOCK cycles and (if registered-feedback) burst cycles.
memory_vs_peripheral_regions.wishbone_peripheral_slave: I/O register block (e.g. Section 8.6 SLAVE I/O Port Examples — Simple 8-bit / 16-bit examples).
memory_vs_peripheral_regions.wishbone_bridge_slave: Other-bus bridge (e.g. WB-to-APB, WB-to-AHB, WB-to-PCI); may use [RTY_O] for temporary unavailability.

slave_classification.memory_slave_general: Decodes [ADR_I()] and serves R/W; supports SINGLE/BLOCK and (optionally) RMW.
slave_classification.fifo_slave: May omit [ADR_I()] (OBSERVATION on page 27); selects via [STB_I]+[CYC_I] only.
slave_classification.dual_port_slave_with_LOCK: Uses [LOCK_I] to hold ownership; [CYC_I] requests use of the common bus from an arbiter.

An interconnection system that supports a single WISHBONE MASTER and a single WISHBONE SLAVE interface. It is the simplest way to connect two cores.

CLK_O / RST_O generated by SYSCON; INTERCON connects CLK_O to all CLK_I and RST_O to all RST_I.

Design INTERCON modules to prevent deadlock conditions. One solution to this problem is to include a watchdog timer function that monitors the MASTER's [STB_O] signal, and asserts [ERR_I] or [RTY_I] if the cycle exceeds some pre-defined time limit. INTERCON modules can also be designed to disconnect interfaces from the WISHBONE bus if they constantly generate bus errors and/or watchdog time-outs.
